stem: Rohan knows a job takes $6$ workers $8$ days. He wants how many days $12$ workers need for the same job.

parts.text: Which claim is correct before any Rule-of-Three calculation?

options.text: Treat workers and days as directly proportional and scale $8$ days by $12/6$.
Reject direct proportion here, because more workers must shorten the time for the same job.
Call the method the Rule of Three and apply it as a direct scale because that label fits.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Workers and days move in opposite directions for a fixed job, so a direct Rule-of-Three scale does not apply.

teacher.key_rationale: More workers shorten days for the same job, so the situation is not direct proportion. A direct scale or the Rule-of-Three label alone is wrong here.
